=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/stale_sessions.py:177-211 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: After the round 1 fix, a single stray valid page shape (`{"data": []}` or any `dict` that `_page` accepts as `([], False, None)`) placed in wrapper text ahead of the real payload is accepted silently. `_page(candidate)` passes, the object is appended to `found`, `len(found) == 1` so no error is raised, and the function returns it as an empty page. The session page and all later pages are never parsed.
  WHY: The pickup processes zero sessions for that page — no archives, no stalls, no error. The next session pages after it (newer sessions on later pages) are also dropped because the function returns the empty page at the first candidate. An operator sees `archived 0; stalls 0` and the finished sessions on that page stay in the session list until the next wake reaches them from the next page.
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/stale_sessions.py:43-49 | severity=low | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: The docstring says "the bare array" is a supported input shape "inside the harness's untrusted-data wrapper text." After the round 1 fix, `_load_document` only accepts `{`-starting lines in wrapper text; a bare array (`[...]`) in wrapper text produces exit 2. The docstring promises a behavior the implementation does not deliver.
  WHY: A reader (or future contributor) relying on the docstring to decide that bare-array wrapper text is safe would discover an exit-2 `no JSON document found` at the first wake. The contract drift is a correctness gap even if bare arrays do not occur in the current harness wrapper format — the docstring is the public contract.
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/stale_sessions.py:43-49 | severity=low | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: The module docstring describes the per-file accepted input shapes as "the `{"ccr": {"data": [...], "has_more", "last_id"}}` object, `{"data": [...]}`, or the bare array, possibly inside the harness's untrusted-data wrapper text (the JSON line is found and parsed; the wrapper is ignored)". After the round 1 fix, the wrapper-text fallback only iterates lines that start with `{` (`if not line.startswith("{"): continue`) and validates each candidate via `_page(candidate)`. A bare array line (e.g. `[{"id": "session_1"}]`) inside wrapper text therefore no longer satisfies the documented contract: it is neither an object line nor a complete-document candidate, so the script exits 2 with `no JSON document found`. The function's own docstring at line 177 ("plain JSON, or the one result object inside the harness wrapper text") correctly captures the round 1 behaviour; the module docstring is the one that drifted.
  WHY: A caller that relies on the module docstring (or that saves a `list_sessions` page whose envelope is a bare array, a shape the module docstring explicitly enumerates) and then wraps it in harness untrusted-data text will trigger exit 2 instead of the documented acceptance. The pickup, which only ever writes pages in object envelopes, will not hit this path; the drift is a contract exposure for any future caller that does.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/stale_sessions.py:177-211 | severity=low | confidence=[2]
  PROBLEM: The wrapper-text fallback accepts any line that starts with `{`, parses as JSON, AND passes `_page(candidate)`. `_page({"data": []})` returns `([], False, None)` — a successful empty-page verdict — so a stray wrapper line that is itself a valid empty page (e.g. a stray `{"data": []}` appearing before the real payload) is silently accepted as an empty result. The script returns zero sessions and zero triggers with exit 0, no `errors` entry, no `archive` entries, and `next_after_id` derived only from the LAST page processed. `test_stray_json_lines_in_wrapper_text_are_not_read_as_the_page` exercises `[]`, `{}`, and `{"note": 1}` as stray lines (all rejected by `_page`) but does not cover the valid-empty-page case.
  WHY: When the harness wrapper text contains a single stray empty-page line, the janitor reports a successful run with zero archives and zero stalls — the same observable signature as a healthy empty run. The known harness wrapper format in the test fixture (`<other-session …>…explanatory text…    {json}</other-session>`) does not produce a stray empty-page line, so this is unlikely in production; it remains a deterministic fail-open edge case the current tests do not pin.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 2
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_7-plus ===
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/stale_sessions.py:190-206 | severity=low | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: The round 1 fix rejects bare-array stray lines (`startswith("{")` filter) and multiple qualifying objects, but a single stray line whose JSON is `{"data": []}` (or any other valid empty page shape) passes `_page` validation and is silently returned as the page. The run then processes zero sessions and zero stalls with exit 0 and no error.
  WHY: A wrapper text whose only qualifying JSON line is a valid empty page shape produces a silent no-op — the pickup reports zero archives and zero stalls, the run looks successful, and nothing is logged. The test `test_stray_json_lines_in_wrapper_text_are_not_read_as_the_page` covers `[]`, `{}`, and `{"note": 1}` as stray lines but not `{"data": []}`, which passes `_page` and is accepted.
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/stale_sessions.py:13-15 | severity=low | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: The module docstring advertises that inputs can be "the bare array, possibly inside the harness's untrusted-data wrapper text." After the round 1 fix, the wrapper-text fallback only accepts lines starting with `{`, so bare arrays in wrapper text are rejected with exit 2 (`no JSON document found`). The plain-JSON path (`json.loads(text)` at the top) still accepts bare arrays, so the docstring is partially correct for plain JSON but wrong for wrapper text.
  WHY: A caller relying on the docstring to pass a bare array inside wrapper text would discover an exit 2 failure rather than the documented acceptance. The failure mode is also worse than documented: the docstring says "the JSON line is found and parsed; the wrapper is ignored," but a bare array in wrapper text is not found and parsed.
=== END FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_7-plus ===
